title: UAE cybersecurity chief says Iranian actors used wipers against UAE systems
summary: At the World Police Summit in Dubai on 18 November, Dr Mohamed Al Kuwaiti, described by The National as the UAE's cybersecurity chief, said Iranian actors used destructive wipers that erase data rather than lock systems for ransom. He said wipers hit electricity, water, desalination, education and healthcare systems, and that AI agents made attack origins hard to trace.
plain: The UAE's cybersecurity chief said Iranian actors used data-destroying malware against UAE electricity, water, desalination, education and healthcare systems, according to The National.
exec: A government says wiper malware, not just ransomware, was used against national infrastructure; plan for destructive attacks.
action: Keep offline, tested backups and rehearse restoring critical systems, since wipers erase data rather than demand ransom.

validation.note: One publisher read; the claim is the official's own speech. No incident dates or forensic detail given.
